ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Data Transfer Object for registering a new member of the Todo List application. Used as the request body when creating a new user account.

This schema maps directly to the 'todo_list_users' Prisma model for core properties. The 'password' property here is the plain-text submission—handled securely by the backend (mapped to 'password_hash' in the DB). Additional fields such as registration connection metadata ('ip', 'href', 'referrer') are required for audit and compliance tracking per AutoBE standard practices.

This DTO is only used during self-registration; admin/system user creation is not supported in this API. All fields must be validated before registration, and system-generated or derived properties must not be accepted in this DTO.

id.description: The unique identifier of the new or authenticated user. Universally unique and directly maps to the 'id' of the user in the database. Must be used as the user's identity in all subsequent requests.

email.description:
Unique email address used for user authentication and identification in the Todo List application.

Email addresses must be unique among all users in the system and are validated upon registration and update. This is the only user credential exposed in the API; passwords are never returned. Used both as the login credential and the contact point for system notifications.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the user account was created.

This field is set automatically at account registration. The value is immutable and provides an audit trail for user onboarding.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) of the most recent update to the user's account profile.

This property is refreshed whenever any user information (such as email or password) is updated. It supports audit requirements and helps detect concurrent modification.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response type for user registration, login, and token refresh. Encapsulates the authenticated user's identity and the JWT tokens required to authorize further requests for the Todo List application.

Returned directly by endpoints that manage user authentication as well as those that establish an authenticated session after registration or login. Client applications must extract and securely store the information from this response to enable authenticated requests and token refresh flows.

This DTO is the single point of authority for issuing, persisting, and rotating access and refresh tokens throughout the user's session lifecycle.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials and session context used by a registered Todo List user to authenticate and obtain JWT authorization tokens.

This DTO is the request body for the user login operation. It requires email (the user's unique login identifier) and raw password, both of which are strictly validated. Session context properties (href, referrer, and optional ip) record the login context for audit purposes, tracking the URL and referrer at the time of authentication.

The password field is always sent in plain text for backend-side hashing and verification, never as a hashed value in the API request. The backend will hash and compare it securely. The 'href' and 'referrer' fields are required and must be provided by the client. Optional 'ip' can be provided by the client or extracted server-side for advanced session tracking.

email.description: Unique email address for user authentication. Must be a valid and previously registered email for this Todo List user. Validated per RFC 5322 email standards.

password.description: Plain-text password associated with this user, used for credential verification at login. Never send hashed passwords in this field; only raw password should be provided for backend-side hashing.

href.description: Connection URL indicating the page from which the user attempted login (current page URL). Required for audit trails and session context tracking. Must be a valid absolute URI.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) from which user navigated to the login form. Required for security and session audits. May be an empty string if direct access.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address for advanced audit and session tracking. May be omitted or set to null for standard use cases. If absent, the backend will extract from request.
Null value if client IP is not specified. Backend will extract IP server-side.

ip.description: Optional field for client-provided IP address during login. Provides enhanced session security and traceability, but is not required by standard login flows.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token payload submitted by an authenticated Todo List user to renew JWT authorization tokens and maintain session continuity.

This DTO serves as the request body for the token refresh endpoint. Requires a valid, non-expired refresh token previously issued during login or registration. Token is validated against backend session policy and revocation checks.

No credential or session context is needed (handled via token validation and cookies). The backend processes the token securely and issues a fresh set of authorization tokens for continued user access.

refresh_token.description: A valid, non-expired refresh token issued to the user on successful login or registration. This string is required to authorize issuance of a new access token. Must be present and valid; absence or expiration triggers error response.

id.description:
Unique system-generated identifier (UUID) for the user. Serves as the primary key for user lookup, authentication, and ownership.

This property ensures that user accounts are globally unique and can be safely referenced across all relational data. It is never mutable after creation.

email.description:
Unique email address used for user authentication and identification in the Todo List application.

Email addresses must be unique among all users in the system and are validated upon registration and update. This is the only user credential exposed in the API; passwords are never returned. Used both as the login credential and the contact point for system notifications.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the user account was created.

This field is set automatically at account registration. The value is immutable and provides an audit trail for user onboarding.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) of the most recent update to the user's account profile.

This property is refreshed whenever any user information (such as email or password) is updated. It supports audit requirements and helps detect concurrent modification.

ITodoListUser.description:
Registered user account in the Todo List application (todo_list_users table).

Represents a unique system user who can authenticate, manage todos, and own their own data, with strict per-user isolation enforced. Exposes only non-sensitive fields: unique ID, email, and timestamps for account creation and updates. Never exposes passwords or authentication hashes in API responses.

email.description:
New email address to assign to the user account. Must be unique across all users in the Todo List application.

Changing this property allows the user to update their primary login credential. The new email is validated for format and uniqueness. If omitted, the email address remains unchanged.

password.description:
Plain text password provided for the purpose of updating user credentials.

This property is required if the user wishes to change their password. It is securely hashed before being persisted in the password_hash column in the database. Never store or return the plain text password. If omitted, the password remains unchanged.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying a registered user's profile fields in todo_list_users.

Allows users to update their email address and/or password. Password is supplied in plain text and will be securely hashed by the backend for storage in the password_hash column of the database. Email changes are subject to format and uniqueness checks. At least one property must be supplied. System fields (id, created_at, updated_at) are not client editable.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Authentication session entity for tracking user login events and access history.

Represents a single session record belonging to a user (from todo_list_users) in the Todo List application. This entity holds metadata for an authenticated session, including client IP address, login entry point (URL), referrer URL, session creation/expiry time, and a reference to the owning user. Session records support audit, diagnostics, and enforcement of session policies across the platform.

Each session is subsidiary to its owning user, providing no independent business identity aside from audit and security analytics context.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the session record. Assigned automatically by the database at creation time and guaranteed unique for each session.

Used as the primary key for referencing, updating, and deleting session records. Keeps integrity with associated user records.

user.description:
Summary of the user account that owns this session record. References the ITodoListUser.ISummary type for efficient business context and avoids the need for additional API calls to reconstruct session/user associations.

Replaces the raw foreign key `todo_list_user_id` in the response type for clarity, context, and single-call atomic operations.

ip.description: Client IP address captured at login time for session creation. Used for security analytics, audit trails, and possible anomaly detection. Required and non-nullable by schema.

href.description: URL of the page or application context where the session was initiated. Used for audit, support, and analytics. Required and non-nullable.

referrer.description: URL that referred the user to the entry/login page when starting this session. Used for historical analysis and referrer-based controls. Required and non-nullable.

created_at.description: Timestamp (RFC 3339 date-time) for when this session was established. Used for audit, support, and time-window-based controls. Non-nullable.

oneOf.description: Timestamp (RFC 3339 date-time) for when the session was closed, expired, or invalidated. Nullable for currently active or indefinite sessions.
Value is null if the session has not yet been closed or expired.

expired_at.description: Timestamp or null for session expiry; required for session lifecycle and security analytics.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Data structure for filtering or searching session records for a given user. Used as the request body for paginated session listing endpoints in the Todo List application.

Includes parameters for pagination, filtering by activity dates, and IP address search. All fields are optional to allow broad or fine-grained queries. Presence of these parameters restricts the returned session set. Designed for audit and diagnostic usage with fully authenticated context.

page.description:
Page number for paginated session listing.
Used for fetching specific pages of the session result set. Defaults to 1 if not provided. Must be positive.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to include in each response page. Used for server-controlled result slicing (pagination). Default is service-administered value; recommended range is 10-100.

ip.description: Filter session records by exact client IP address. Used for IP-based investigation, anomaly detection, or audit. If omitted, no filtering by IP is applied.

href.description: Filter sessions by the login entry URL. Allows narrowing session listings to those created from a specific application or context page. If omitted, all URLs are included.

referrer.description: Filter sessions by referrer URL. Permits audit or listing of sessions started from specific referrers. If omitted, all referrers are included.

created_from.description: Minimum (inclusive) lower bound for session creation timestamp (RFC 3339 format). Allows filtering for sessions created after a certain time. If omitted, there is no lower-bound constraint.

created_to.description: Maximum (inclusive) upper-bound for session creation timestamp. Enables filtering for sessions created before or on a certain time. If omitted, there is no upper-bound constraint.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Represents a single todo item owned by a registered user of the application.

Each todo is characterized by a non-empty, required title with a maximum of 255 characters, an optional description up to 1000 characters, a boolean completion status, and automatic timestamps tracking creation and modification dates (created_at, updated_at). Every todo must belong to a unique user (user_id), which is resolved from the authenticated actor context—not accepted from API requests. No soft deletion or historical records are maintained, and todos are fully isolated by owner; only the user who created the todo may access, update, or delete it. The model does not allow for any form of user delegation, impersonation, or teaming.

No other domain entities relate to the todo except strict ownership; enforcement is via the user_id foreign key constraint to the todo_list_users model. All permissions, privacy, and CRUD operations for the MVP are governed by this core type.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. Assigned automatically upon creation. Used for all retrieval, update, and deletion operations.

title.description: Title of the todo item. Must be non-empty and a maximum of 255 characters. Required for task creation and updates.

description.description: Optional detailed description of the todo item. When provided, must not exceed 1000 characters. May be omitted or null for simple tasks.

completed.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the todo item is marked as completed (true) or still pending (false). Managed entirely by the task's owner.

created_at.description: Timestamp representing when the todo item was created. Set automatically on insertion; immutable.

updated_at.description: Timestamp representing the last time the todo item was updated. Automatically refreshed on every change.

user.description: The owning user for this todo item, transformed from the internal user_id field. Always points to the authenticated actor who created and manages this task.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
The data transfer object for creating a new todo item. Used in the request body of the POST /todoList/user/todos endpoint.

This schema represents the minimal information required by business logic to create a todo owned by the authenticated user. Only the owner may create their own todos; ownership context is enforced via authentication and the backend never allows user_id to be set in the request.

Every todo must include a non-empty title up to 255 characters, optionally a description up to 1000 characters, and (if supported by business logic) an optional due date as a valid future ISO 8601 date-time string. Completion status is never accepted from the request; it is always set to false by default. All timestamps are managed automatically by the backend. Any violation of constraints will cause validation errors. The schema directly corresponds to the todo_list_todos table in the database, but strictly omits system fields, actor fields, and system timestamps from the request.

title.description: The title of the todo item. Required, must not be blank, limited to 255 characters as enforced by business rules and the database.

oneOf.description: Optional description for the todo item. If present, cannot exceed 1000 characters.
Description can be omitted or set to null if not provided.

description.description: Optional description for the todo item. Limited to 1000 characters if provided; may be null if not provided. If present, subject to all business and database constraints.

oneOf.description: Optional due date for the todo. Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string representing a future point in time if supplied.
Due date can be omitted or set to null if not provided.

due_date.description: Optional due date. When present, must be an ISO 8601 date-time string and must represent a time in the future. Not required; can be omitted or null.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
The data transfer object for updating an existing todo item. Used in the request body of the PUT /todoList/user/todos/{todoId} endpoint.

Represents any subset of updatable todo fields, subject to strict validation and business rules. Used only to update the todo item owned by the currently authenticated user (user_id must never be present or accepted in the request). Each field (title, description, completed, due_date) is optional, but at least one must be provided and valid to constitute a legal update. The backend enforces all field constraints on update as with creation.

Upon successful update, the system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp and retains full ownership context. Fields with null type may be cleared by setting null, otherwise updated as allowed. All remaining fields not provided retain previous values. The schema matches updateable fields on the todo_list_todos table, excluding system-managed and actor fields.

title.description: The new title for the todo item. If provided, must not be blank and must not exceed 255 characters.

oneOf.description: The new description for the todo. If provided, cannot exceed 1000 characters.
Used to clear the description, setting it to null.

description.description: The new description for the todo item. May be updated, truncated, or cleared (set to null). Limited to 1000 characters if present.

completed.description: Completion status of the todo. True indicates completion; false indicates the task remains open. Optional and only modifiable by the owner.

oneOf.description: The new due date. Must be an ISO 8601 date-time string for a future date/time if provided.
Used to clear the due date, setting it to null.

due_date.description: The updated due date for the todo. If present, must be a valid ISO 8601 future date-time or null to clear. Optional.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a single todo item as displayed in todo list and reference contexts.

Provides essential overview information for a todo belonging to a registered user, including the unique identifier, title, completion status, and creation timestamp. Summary objects are optimized for list rendering and are included in references from other entities. All fields derive directly from the corresponding database schema with no additional aggregations or computed fields.

Used in search results, feed endpoints, and in relationship reference objects such as parent or child summaries. This type must be lightweight, omitting detailed, large, or composition-based data. Security and privacy rules are strictly enforced, ensuring no sensitive user data or internal fields are exposed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. Matches the primary key as defined in the database schema. This value is globally unique and used to reference or manipulate the specific todo item via API operations.

title.description: Title of the todo item. Non-empty, up to 255 characters in length. Required for both creation and summary display. Sourced directly from the database with validation rules enforcing non-blank strings.

completed.description: Indicates whether the todo item is marked as complete (true) or not (false). The completion state can only be changed by the owning user. This field is used for UI checkbox displays and status filtering in API queries.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the todo was first created, as recorded in the database. This value is set by the system and is immutable post-creation. Used to sort, filter, and display historical todo activity, always in RFC 3339/ISO8601 format for proper timezone support.

user.description: Summary reference to the owning user who created and owns this todo. Only the minimal identifying properties necessary for list views and context embedding are included. Full user data is accessible via detail API calls when needed.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for searching and filtering todos based on flexible query criteria.

This structure supports full CRUD search, filtering, and paginated result requests for user-managed todo items. Filtering criteria include substring search in the title, completion status, and update or creation date windows. Pagination and sorting options are always present. All requests are validated to ensure users may only query their own or explicitly permitted records; no cross-user searches are ever allowed in MVP.

The schema is designed for maximum search and UI flexibility, supporting all typical dashboard and list screen user workflows. Pagination and sorting allow for scalable performance even with large todo datasets.

search.description:
Search phrase applied across the title, description, or content fields of user todos.

Supports partial (substring) matching, case insensitivity, and can be used for quick filtering in large todo collections. Useful for dashboard search features and every part of the list or filter UI.

completed.description: Filter criterion by completion status. If true, returns only completed todos; if false, only incomplete ones. If omitted, includes both completed and incomplete items. This matches all completion tracking UIs and analytics.

created_from.description:
Start datetime for filtering todos created on or after this timestamp. Must be in ISO 8601 format.

Allows the user to see todos created since a specific point in time, as may be needed for period-based report generation or activity tracking.

created_to.description:
End datetime for filtering todos created before or up to this timestamp. Must be in ISO 8601 format.

Used for retrieving todos created before a cutoff, supporting time-based reporting and analytics.

updated_from.description:
